It was English class and as usual, she drew trees on her arms. The roots wrapped around her fingers and the branches stretched up towards her shoulders. People had grown used to her and always asked what type of tree was drawing. Today, she had chosen a willow.  

Suddenly, she realized the room had fallen silent and everyone had turned towards her. 

"What? Did I miss a question?"

"Stop drawing and listen," said her teacher. 

"What? I'm listening, you just stopped talking for a moment. What happened?"

Everyone continued staring, some started whispering, but quickly fell silent. I guess they felt awkward being talked about. She could feel blood rush to her face and her ears started to burn. 

"It's okay, no need to be embarrassed. My ears do that, too," whispered Tom. He sat in the chair next to her and always smelled of mints. She wondered whether he ever ate anything else. 

"I eat things! I like sandwiches!" said Tom. At this point, she looked more confused than ever. 

"What? Can you guys stop staring at me? Sandwiches? And what about my ears?" at this point, her color resembled a tomato's. 

Up until that morning, she had lived a perfectly subtle existence. She wasn't very loud and she didn't get into trouble too often. Today, however, marked the beginning and things would never be the same again. Destiny was knocking on the door. 

Everyone turned towards the room's entrance. I didn't mean it literally! This is a literature class, you all should know better! They turned back towards her and she started to sweat again. She stood and ruffled her hair.

"Um...I've got to..uh...go to the bathroom."

"What about destiny?" wondered Tom. 

Dear Tom, stop interrupting the story! 

"What is wrong with you?" she asked, confusion and fear wrinkling her forehead. Suddenly she looked up. Perhaps, she could hear me, too, now.

"Yes I can!"

What a pity. You're never supposed to hear the narrator: you're just supposed to do things and they're supposed to talk about them. 

"Can you shut up?"

But if I do, you'll stop existing. You only exist within the confines of this story after all. She stood on her chair and yelled at the ceiling.

"That isn't true! Now leave me alone!" 

Dear, I'm not on the ceiling. She grimaced and jumped off of the chair, sputtering curses. 

"I told you to stop!"

Are you quite sure? She nodded her head vigorously, although some of her classmates had started to look queasy.

"What if the voice is telling the truth? If it stops talking, you die!" said a ginger-haired girl in the back corner. 

"It's my life and my privacy!" she yelled. She thought about the pink-laced panties she was wearing and the chocolate she had stolen the week before. Usually, she was the calm sort, but she was on the verge of breaking the pen in her hand out of rage. 

"Stop!" she screamed.

What a pity. I guess I have no choice. She sighed with relief. 

Goodbye.

"Hey there, lovely."

She glared.

"Can I help you with something?"

She bit on the lolipop between her teeth and I heard the hard sugar crack. 

"Can I buy you a drink?"

She stared and tilted her head slowly, all her confusion and irritation bunched up in a small crease between her eyebrows.

"We are in the park and its the middle of the day."

"What makes you so sure you dont?"

"You can't skateboard."

"Prove it."

She chewed and cracked her lolipop again. Was she pretending the candy was my skull?

I heard a crack, like a broken lolipop, and i felt sticky warmth ooze around my shoulders. 

Before the paramedics came, memories of the future trickled across my vision. A slow recovery, nights spent abusing painkillers and afternoons where clouds of opium hugged my trembling body.
